title: Canary Replay Driver, Throughput Fingerprinting, and Acceptance Runbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a repeatable canary replay driver and a throughput-fingerprinting methodology to validate Dedicated capacity commitments for customers. Produce an operational runbook and an acceptance checklist that customer success and onboarding teams can execute to sign off on SLA guarantees.
background: Customers booking Dedicated pools need predictable throughput and autoscaling behavior for mixed workloads. Existing synthetic probes either overfit to microbenchmarks or fail to reproduce KV-cache and prefix effects seen in production. This initiative creates a middle-ground approach: capture representative request traces (fingerprints), synthesize high-fidelity replay workloads that exercise batching, KV cache warmup, kernel-selection variance, and autoscaler triggers, and provide a deterministic acceptance flow for customer signoff.
goals: Provide a lightweight replay driver that can run inside customer-dedicated env or in our lab
Define a throughput fingerprint format and golden baseline for each supported model-family
Automate acceptance checks that map observed metrics to contract pass/fail
Integrate results into Console dashboards and generate a standardized signoff artifact
scope: Includes: trace capture tooling, a portable replay driver, fingerprint schema, benchmark harness, runbook, and Console integration. Excludes: long-term storage of raw customer traces (handled by a separate compliance project) and per-customer custom model tuning.
approach: Trace capture: lightweight sampling on production routes to create anonymized request fingerprints (prompt length, temperature, model, prefix tokens, KV usage flags)
Seed generation: expand fingerprints into replay input streams with probability distributions for prompt lengths and user think-times
Distributed replay: orchestrate replay drivers across a small fleet to emulate realistic client concurrency and burst patterns
Autoscaler exercise: include synthetic load patterns that trigger scale-up and scale-down paths to validate policy boundaries
Baseline comparison: compare current run to golden fingerprint (tokens/sec, p99/p95 tails, KV cache hit rate, fail-rate) and compute pass/fail
Safety & throttle: sandbox replays in customer lab with guardrails to prevent noisy neighbor effects
test_scenarios: Steady-state: 500 concurrent clients sending short-chat prompts to evaluate sustained tokens/sec and p95 latency
Burst + cooldown: 10x burst for 60s followed by gradual cooldown to test autoscaler hysteresis
Cold-cache heavy: replay sequences that invalidate KV cache to measure cold-start tail latency
Mixed model workload: 70% small-reply model, 30% long-context generation to observe kernel-switching overhead
Fault injection: simulate slow backend disks / transient GPU throttling to validate graceful degradation policies
tooling: k6 & locust scripts for client-side load patterns
s3-compatible artifact store for fingerprints and run artifacts
notebook templates (Python) for quick result analysis
runbook_steps: 1) Prepare environment: deploy replay-driver to target cluster and ensure appropriate RBAC and quotas
2) Upload fingerprint: select pre-approved fingerprint or produce one via trace-capture (anonymized)
3) Configure run: set duration, concurrency profile, and autoscaler policy to test
4) Dry run: execute low-intensity smoke replay and validate metrics pipeline
5) Full replay: run target scenario capturing all metrics and logs
6) Post-process: compute delta vs golden baseline and produce pass/fail report
7) Signoff: attach artifacts to Console run and request Customer Success review
8) Remediation: if failed, collect diagnostic bundle (profiles, sampler logs) and open triage ticket
customer_acceptance_checklist: Observed sustained tokens/sec >= contract target for primary model-family (within 5% variance)
p99 latency under agreed threshold for 95% of supported routes
No cascading fail modes observed during autoscaler activity
KV cache warmup behavior documented and within accepted tail SLA
Run artifacts uploaded and accessible by customer success and engineering
Any remediation items have owner and ETA declared
risks: Replay fidelity mismatch: synthetic inputs may not capture real-world client behavior
Noisy neighbor interference when running in shared lab clusters
Autoscaler nondeterminism causing flaky pass/fail across runs
Customer privacy concerns around trace collection
mitigations: Fingerprint design includes statistical distributions to better reflect variability
Prefer isolated lab namespaces or run inside customer-dedicated pool with explicit consent
Repeat runs and require median-of-3 for final acceptance decision
Capture only metadata and anonymized token lengths; PII redaction step enforced
progress_updates: 2025-11-10: Spec drafted and reviewed with PM and SRE. Decided on fingerprint schema v1 (length, model_id, kv_flag, interarrival_ms). Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Throughput+Fingerprinting
2026-01-18: Benchmarks in lab-1 showed consistent tokens/sec within 8% of synthetic baseline. Logged known variance around cold-cache scenarios.
2026-02-22: Integrated run artifacts with Console test-results view (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/802). Initial runbook draft shared with Customer Success for feedback.
2026-03-10: Pilot accepted by two customers in staging. Minor autoscaler policy adjustments scheduled (ENG-22111).
notes: Aim for the fingerprint schema to be compact (under 1KB per sample) so artifacts are easy to move between customer environments. Next milestone: formalize golden baselines for top 6 models and publish to docs.
